chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from Abī Hammām, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd ibn Ghazwān, from al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, from Abū Dharr رضي الله عنه: that he came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and said:

O Messenger of Allah, I am ruined; I had intercourse without water. He said: so the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله ordered for a litter, and I concealed myself with it, and for water, so I performed ghusl, I and she. Then he said to me: “O Abā Dharr, the earth suffices you for ten years.”

(562) 36. As for the report narrated by al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said: I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: if he finds water after having prayed with tayammum while he is within the time? He said: “His salat is complete, and there is no repetition upon him.”

The meaning in it is that when he prayed with tayammum, he was within the time; it does not mean that when he found water, he was still within the time. For if, at the time he found the water, the time still remained, then repeating the salat would have been obligatory upon him according to what has preceded.

(563) 37. Likewise, the report narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from Yaʿqūb ibn Sālim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: concerning a man who performed tayammum and prayed, then found water while he was within the time, he said: “His salat has passed, and he should purify himself.”

So it may bear what we mentioned: that when he performed tayammum and prayed, he was within the time, not that when he found water the time still remained. And it is also possible that what is meant is that he found water while he was within the time, except that he had not yet completed the salat in full, and had only prayed one rakʿah or two rakʿahs of it; so he said, “His salat has passed,” meaning what he had already prayed of it. As for his statement, “and he should purify himself,” it is to be understood as meaning that he should purify himself for another salat that he will begin.

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ: repetition or re-performance of the salat
key_terms.اغْتَسَلْتُ: I performed ghusl, the ritual bath
key_terms.الصَّعِيدُ: the earth or clean ground used for tayammum
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, whose availability affects the ruling of tayammum
key_terms.الْوَقْتِ: the prescribed time of the salat
key_terms.تَيَمُّمٍ: dry ablution performed in place of wudu or ghusl when water is unavailable
key_terms.يَتَطَهَّرْ: let him purify himself, meaning to attain ritual purity

ai.seo_question: If someone prays with tayammum and then finds water within the prayer time, must the salat be repeated?
ai.summary: This passage reports the hadith of Abū Dharr رضي الله عنه regarding intercourse in the absence of water and the sufficiency of tayammum, then cites two further reports about one who prayed with tayammum and later found water. The accompanying explanation reconciles the reports by clarifying the timing of finding water and whether the prayer had already been completed.
